analysis.root_cause: Most skills are prompt-only: they define behavior via .claude/commands/*.md files but have no code-level implementation file that governance validators can enforce. The 7 skills with paths are supervisor infrastructure tools that happen to exist as Python scripts.
analysis.enforcement_gap: Without implementation_paths, the skill registry cannot verify that a skill invocation actually ran the correct code. Skills become advisory-only behavior guides rather than enforced code pathways.
analysis.risk: HIGH — skill adoption can be claimed without actual code execution. evidence-quality-closeout.json REC-B-001 demonstrates this: 7 items, 0 actual skill transcripts, adoption_compliance_status=FAIL.

recommended_actions.action: Mark all 55 active prompt-only skills as advisory_only=true in the registry
recommended_actions.rationale: Honest classification prevents false adoption compliance claims

recommended_actions.action: Add implementation_paths to the top 10 most-used skills (add-python-api, add-dotnet-api, add-roundtrip-test, score-format, check-gate, package-install-proof, record-lane-execution, validate-product-code-ledger, preflight-skill-entry, sal-pipeline-heal)
recommended_actions.rationale: These skills have the highest execution frequency and greatest impact on product quality
recommended_actions.effort: MEDIUM — requires creating or identifying the backing Python/bash scripts

recommended_actions.action: Add V49 governance validator: if adoption_compliance_status=FAIL and skill_transcripts=0, block sprint if >3 PRODUCT_SOURCE items
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents silent skill adoption FAIL from not blocking continuation
